classification.difficultyReason: Determine the second multiplier from the desired overall change, using the increased quantity as the percentage base.

content.prompt: A quantity is increased by 10%. What further percentage change, applied to the increased value, is required to produce these changes relative to the original quantity?

answer.worked:
The combined multiplier must be $1.32$.
$$\begin{align*}\text{Further multiplier}&=\frac{1.32}{1.10}\\\text{Further multiplier}&=1.20\\\text{Further percentage change}&=(1.20-1)\times100\%\\\text{Further percentage change}&=20\%\end{align*}$$
A 20% increase is required.

The combined multiplier must be $1.155$.
$$\begin{align*}\text{Further multiplier}&=\frac{1.155}{1.10}\\\text{Further multiplier}&=1.05\\\text{Further percentage change}&=(1.05-1)\times100\%\\\text{Further percentage change}&=5\%\end{align*}$$
A 5% increase is required.

The combined multiplier must be $0.88$.
$$\begin{align*}\text{Further multiplier}&=\frac{0.88}{1.10}\\\text{Further multiplier}&=0.80\\\text{Further percentage decrease}&=(1-0.80)\times100\%\\\text{Further percentage decrease}&=20\%\end{align*}$$
A 20% decrease is required.

The combined multiplier must be $0.935$.
$$\begin{align*}\text{Further multiplier}&=\frac{0.935}{1.10}\\\text{Further multiplier}&=0.85\\\text{Further percentage decrease}&=(1-0.85)\times100\%\\\text{Further percentage decrease}&=15\%\end{align*}$$
A 15% decrease is required.
